steps.name: Differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: With n=6 per group and raw salmon counts, dispersion estimates will be noisy for low-count genes; the prefilter and BH correction are the safeguards
Any gene in the significant list may be responding to the B2 processing conditions rather than the treatment — the analysis has no power to tell these apart
LFC shrinkage (apeglm) affects point estimates, not p-values; never report shrunk LFC alongside unshrunk p-values as if they were one coherent model without saying so
steps.context: Uses the size factors and VST matrix from T1S1. The contrast tested is treated vs control and is statistically identical to B2 vs B1; no design in any software can split it. DESeq2 1.52.0 and apeglm 1.34.0 are installed.
steps.question: Which genes change between treated and control samples, quantified as the combined treated-vs-control and B2-vs-B1 effect, with FDR control and shrunk effect sizes?
constraints: Run DESeq2 with design = ~ condition and contrast = treated vs control; never add batch to the design (it is collinear and the model matrix is rank-deficient)
Prefilter low-count genes (e.g., require a minimal normalized count in a minimal number of samples) and report how many of the 12,000 genes survive
Apply BH multiple-testing correction and apeglm log2FC shrinkage for reporting effect sizes; report the number of genes at FDR < 0.05 and < 0.1
Title every output table and figure so that the contrast is labeled 'treatment + batch (confounded)' rather than 'treatment effect'
steps.description: DESeq2 differential expression on the raw counts with the only identifiable design (~ condition), contrast treated vs control, with effect-size shrinkage and explicit labeling of the estimate as the combined treatment+batch effect.
acceptance_criteria: Full DE results table (gene symbol, baseMean, log2FC shrunk, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) written as CSV, with a header/README line stating the design was ~ condition and that effects are confounded with batch
Summary counts of significant genes (padj < 0.05 and padj < 0.1) and of genes with |log2FC| > 1
MA plot and volcano plot saved as PNGs with the confounding caveat in the caption/title
Number of genes dropped by prefiltering and number entering the test reported

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the shifted genes
caveats: The ranked list carries the batch+condition confounding, so pathway hits may reflect a B2 processing artifact rather than drug/treatment biology; this limitation must appear in the output, not just in the analyst's head
Gene symbols may contain version suffixes or whitespace — normalize both sides before matching
If the mapping rate is very low (<50% of tested genes matched), report it prominently rather than interpreting the enrichment
steps.context: The DE step (T1S2) produces a full ranked list over ~12,000 gene symbols. A human pathway gene set collection in HGNC gene-symbol GMT format (WikiPathways) is available in the reference store; the executing agent resolves it against the environment. fgsea 1.38.0 is installed in the R track.
steps.question: Which human pathways are coordinately shifted among the genes ranked by the treated-vs-control (batch+condition combined) statistic?
constraints: Use a preranked test (fgsea) on the full ranked list rather than an over-representation test on a cutoff-derived list, so the result does not depend on an arbitrary FDR threshold
Report both NES and BH-adjusted q-value; do not interpret pathways with q >= 0.25 as hits
Match on HGNC symbols; report the fraction of ranked genes that map to any gene set
State in the output that enriched pathways reflect the joint treatment+batch signal and cannot be attributed to the treatment alone
steps.description: Preranked GSEA (fgsea) of the DE-ranked gene list against human WikiPathways gene sets in HGNC symbols, characterizing the biology of the shifted genes with the confounding caveat carried through.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked gene list (gene symbol, signed Wald statistic from T1S2) written to file
GSEA results table (pathway name, WikiPathways ID, size, NES, pval, padj/BH q) for all tested pathways with nonzero size
Report of how many of the 12,000 input genes mapped to the GMT and how many pathways passed the minimum set-size filter
Interpretation text labels the hits as characterizing the combined treated/B2-vs-control/B1 signal, not treatment-specific biology

plan.title: Treated-vs-control DE under confounded batch
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbols) from human lung, 6 treated vs 6 control. The profile states the critical design fact: every treated sample was processed in batch B2 and every control in batch B1, so condition and batch are perfectly confounded. No statistical model can estimate a treatment effect separate from a batch effect here — a design with both terms is rank-deficient. The plan therefore (1) normalizes with DESeq2 size factors and characterizes the global structure (PCA, sample distances) to make the confounding visible in the output; (2) runs differential expression with DESeq2 using the only identifiable design, ~ condition, contrasting treated vs control, and reports every result explicitly as the combined treatment+batch effect, with BH FDR and apeglm-shrunk log2FC; (3) characterizes the shifted genes with preranked fgsea against human WikiPathways gene sets (HGNC symbols, matching the gene-symbol row names directly), again framed as the combined signal. No step attempts batch correction, because with one batch per condition there is nothing to estimate it from; that limitation is stated in every output rather than papered over.
